findings.title: Priority-0 mail can spend the whole Resend day quota, leaving no room for the owner's sign-in codes and delaying receipts (the buyer's only link) for hours
findings.evidence: outbox_claim: `v_sent_today < p_daily_quota - case o.priority when 0 then 0 when 1 then p_reserve else p_reserve + p_low_reserve end` — priority 0 (receipt, order_shipped, order_refunded, order_ready, owner_alert × each active owner) stops only at 100. Sign-in codes go through Supabase Auth's Resend SMTP (PLANS/ISSUES.md I28) and are not counted; docs/operations.md:270-276 says the 20-send reserve 'must absorb auth traffic too', but the reserve is held back from everything but priority 0. Resend: 'daily email quota of 100 emails/day' with no SMTP/API distinction (fetched 2026-10-06).
findings.impact: On a day with >=100 priority-0 sends (about 50 paid orders: one receipt + one shipped notice each, plus alerts to every owner) Resend answers daily_quota_exceeded for the rest of the UTC day: an owner whose session expired cannot get a sign-in code (locked out of /admin while orders flow), and every later receipt waits until 00:00 UTC, so buyers of digital books who closed the return tab cannot reach their order page or file for hours; recovery links (priority 1, stops at 80) are held too. Precondition: the free-plan sizing the contract (section 8) assumes.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep a small floor for auth below which priority 0 also stops (new parameter p_auth_reserve, e.g. 5, so priority 0 stops at p_daily_quota - p_auth_reserve), and have the owner decide on a paid Resend plan before launch and raise DAILY_QUOTA accordingly; put the per-day order capacity into the launch checklist.
findings.prior_overlap: AUDIT-1 S04.1 ('the last 20 are kept for codes and receipts') and docs/operations.md 'Sign-in codes share the account' residual; worse than recorded because P08 moved five mail kinds into the tier that ignores the reserve

findings.title: A buyer whose address is wrong or suppressed has no way to reach a paid order, and staff have no action to correct the address, lift the suppression or reissue the link
findings.evidence: The only link path is mail to orders.customer_email (receipt in order_try_commit; `order_link` in order_recover_apply, delivery.sql:252-254). A hard bounce or a complaint inserts the address hash into finance.email_suppressions (audit2_fixes.sql:653) and outbox_claim marks every later row to it `suppressed` (order_emails.sql:277-282); no function deletes a suppression, no staff function changes an order's customer_email/email_hash, and order_detail deliberately exposes no token or idempotency key. docs/operations.md 'A lost link' (797-803) and 'Suppression' (290-301: 'a deliberate manual database action') give no recipe for either case.
findings.impact: A buyer who mistyped the address at checkout, or whose first receipt hard-bounced, has paid (often for a digital book) and can never open the order page or download the file; when he writes through the contact form Anas sees the order but has no button, function or documented SQL to fix the address or send the link, so the case ends in a refund or an ad-hoc database edit.
findings.proposed_fix: One owner action (fresh TOTP) `order_contact_set(p_order, p_email)` that rewrites customer_email and email_hash under the order lock, audits the change without the address, and queues one `order_link` row for the new address; plus a documented, tested SQL recipe for lifting a suppression (`delete from finance.email_suppressions where recipient_hash = finance.recipient_hash($1)`). Until built, write the manual recipe into docs/operations.md.

findings.title: A full refund of a preorder line that has already shipped releases its reservation and frees capacity for a copy that left the shelf
findings.evidence: refund_succeed (the replaced version that runs): `update finance.inventory_reservations x set state = 'released' ... where x.order_id = v_order.id and x.preorder and x.state <> 'released' and x.variant_id in (select i.variant_id ... where coalesce(finance.item_fully_refunded(i.id), false))` — no condition on finance.fulfillments.state. finance.preorder_committed (payment_core.sql:445-447) counts only `state = 'committed'`, so the released unit is sellable again.
findings.impact: While a variant is still a preorder, a goodwill refund (no return) of a shipped preorder copy lowers preorder_committed by its quantity, so one more copy than exists can be preordered; the stock rule for ordinary lines is the opposite ('shipped stock is not restored'). Bounded: preorder is off at opening (Q05) and variants are normally switched to stock when copies arrive.
findings.proposed_fix: Release the preorder reservation only for lines with no fulfilment row in ('shipped','delivered') (digital lines and unshipped physical lines): add `and not exists (select 1 from finance.fulfillments f join finance.order_items i2 on i2.id = f.order_item_id where i2.order_id = x.order_id and i2.variant_id = x.variant_id and f.state in ('shipped','delivered'))`; a shipped copy comes back only through return_receive.

findings.title: A carrier or tracking value mistyped at «تم الشحن» cannot be corrected: shipped→shipped with other values is BAD_TRANSITION and the wrong number is what the buyer was mailed
findings.evidence: `when 'shipped' then f.state = 'preparing' or (f.state = 'shipped' and f.carrier is not distinct from v_carrier and f.tracking is not distinct from v_tracking)` — only an identical repeat passes; any other carrier/tracking on a shipped line answers BAD_TRANSITION (683). The `order_shipped` mail (721-724) and order_access carry the fulfilment row's values.
findings.impact: One typo in a tracking number (a long Latin/digit string typed in an RTL form) leaves the buyer's order page and the shipping mail pointing at a wrong parcel for the life of the order; the owner's only remedy is a database edit.
findings.proposed_fix: Allow `shipped` → `shipped` with new carrier/tracking as a correction (same version bump and audit row) and queue a second `order_shipped` mail keyed on the new values (e.g. `order_shipped:<orderId>:<md5(items)>:<md5(carrier|tracking)>`) so the buyer receives the corrected number.

findings.title: A refund parked MODE_CHANGED stays in flight for ever: no function can settle or close it, and it blocks refunds of that payment
findings.evidence: payment_reconcile_claim: `update finance.refunds r set next_check_at = null, error = 'MODE_CHANGED' ... where r.status in ('submitting','uncertain')` keeps the status in flight. The only exits are refund_result/refund_settle (both need a successful fetch with the configured key, which answers 404 for the other mode: refunds.ts:269-270 → 503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE) and refund_checked (never closes). refund_request/refund_record_external on that payment answer REFUND_IN_FLIGHT (refunds.sql:421-423, 748-750).
findings.impact: After the test→live switch any test refund in flight at that moment is a permanent «قيد التحقق» row under «تحتاج مطابقة»; the contract says 'a person settles it from the dashboard' but gives the person no function to record the outcome in the ledger (round 6 open risk 5 was never closed).
findings.proposed_fix: Give the owner a way to close a MODE_CHANGED refund by hand: either refund_settle accepts a manual outcome for rows whose error is MODE_CHANGED (owner, fresh TOTP, audit `refund.closed_manually`), or the claim fails such refunds outright (status failed, balance free) and alerts the owners once.

findings.title: A receipt that leaves after the order was refunded tells the buyer the payment is 'being reviewed'
findings.evidence: renderReceipt: `if (order.status !== 'paid') { ... 'وصلتنا دفعتك للطلب رقم X بمبلغ Y، ونراجع الطلب الآن.' }` — the same sentence for paid_needs_resolution and for `refunded`; order_email_data reads the live status at send time, and a receipt held by the quota (priority 0 stops only at 100) or a provider outage can leave after the refund.
findings.impact: The buyer receives «استرداد من طلبك» and then a receipt saying the order is under review; a confusing pair that invites a support message. Precondition: a refund before the receipt leaves.
findings.proposed_fix: Branch on `refunded` in renderReceipt: either close the row (`closed('REFUNDED')`, left out of outbox_attention like NO_FILE) or render one line stating the payment arrived and was refunded, with the refunded total.
findings.prior_overlap: R5-04 fixed the file note for this case; the status sentence was left

findings.title: Where the refund step-up lives: enforced only in the admin Edge Function; the SQL rechecks the owner role but not aal2, and the Data API cannot reach the refund functions at all
findings.evidence: handleAdmin: `if (!staff.recentTotp) return fail(403, 'STEP_UP_REQUIRED', ...)` for refund-create and refund-record-external; recentTotp = hasRecentTotp(claims) (aal2 and a totp amr entry within 300 s, recent-totp.ts:8-19) from claims verified by auth.getClaims (staff.ts:36). refund_request/refund_record_external check only an active owner for p_actor (refunds.sql:344-348, 701-705) and are revoked from public/anon/authenticated, granted to service_role (827-839); refunds.test.ts:433 and refunds-http.test.ts:742 prove the 42501 and the 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED.
findings.impact: No defect: the gate holds as designed. Recorded because a future grant of a refund function to `authenticated` would silently drop the step-up (the SQL has no aal2 check of its own).
findings.proposed_fix: None required; optionally assert `(select auth.jwt() ->> 'aal') = 'aal2'` inside the owner recheck when auth.uid() is not null.

findings.title: Refund amount boundaries: 1 halala is accepted by the ledger while Moyasar documents no minimum; a refused minimum ends cleanly as `failed`
findings.evidence: `p_amount < 1` raises; 1 is accepted and reserved; refunds.ts halalas = z.number().int().positive(). docs.moyasar.com/api/payments/05-refund-payment (fetched 2026-10-06) says only 'less than our equal to the payment amount (or captured)'. A 4xx from the provider becomes refund_fail REFUND_REFUSED (refunds.ts:180-182, refunds.sql:534-535) and frees the balance. 0 → 422; exactly the remainder → order `refunded`; above → EXCEEDS_BALANCE (442-444).
findings.impact: No wrong state either way; if the sandbox refuses small amounts the owner sees «تعذّر تنفيذ الإجراء» without the reason.
findings.proposed_fix: Record the sandbox answer in the runbook (E02 item 8); if a minimum exists, refuse below it in refund_request with its own code and Arabic sentence.
findings.proof_recipe: With the real sandbox key and a paid test payment: POST /v1/payments/<id>/refund {"amount": 1}; expect 200 with refunded = 1, or a 400 naming the minimum.

plan_gaps.title: Mail capacity for the launch: the free Resend plan (100/day) is sized for a quiet store, not a book launch, and no gate asks the owner to choose a plan or a per-day order ceiling
plan_gaps.why_needed: Every paid order queues at least one priority-0 mail (the receipt, the buyer's only order link) and usually a second (order_shipped); owner alerts multiply by the number of owners; sign-in codes share the account. At about 50 orders a day the outbox stops, later buyers wait until 00:00 UTC for their link and file, and an owner whose session expired cannot sign in. Contract section 8 and docs/operations.md record the limit; nothing in P11 asks for the decision.
plan_gaps.touches: PLANS/WORK-PACKAGES.md P11 and the launch checklist; supabase/functions/_shared/outbox.ts DAILY_QUOTA/RESERVE; 20261002120000_order_emails.sql outbox_claim

plan_gaps.title: A staff path for a buyer whose address is wrong or suppressed: correct the order's address, lift a suppression, reissue the link
plan_gaps.why_needed: The order link travels only by mail to orders.customer_email; a typo at checkout or a hard bounce leaves a paid buyer of a digital book with no way in and staff with no function or documented SQL (DB-POST-03). Support will meet this in the first week.

plan_gaps.title: Life cycle of superseded paid files: what earlier buyers get when a new file replaces a variant's file, and when the old object leaves Storage

A corrected edition cannot be pushed to buyers who already hold an entitlement, and no admin action removes a superseded object. Anas should decide whether a replacement reaches existing buyers.
